articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Voltage Overshoot in Bidirectional Phase-Shift Full Bridge Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: To achieve high power density and efficiency in an isolated bidirectional DC/DC converter on DC microgrid, bidirectional phase-shift full bridge (PSFB) converter is employed in this paper. However, the PSFB converter exhibits a significant voltage overshoot on the secondary side of the transformer, which increases the voltage stress on secondary side switches. This paper proposes a simplified model to predict and characterize this voltage overshoot and explains the detailed circuit operation, as well as the corresponding mathematical derivations. The model can be used to evaluate the voltage overshoot and explore voltage suppression techniques, providing insights into the circuit behaviors.

articleTitle: Self-Powered and Self-Controlled Hybrid DC Circuit Breaker for Low Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Current research and development on DC circuit breakers (DCCB) are on (i) mechanical (ii) solid state and (iii) hybrid. Each type has its own advantages and disadvantages. In the case of solid-state or hybrid DCCBs where semiconductor switches are utilised, additional circuitry are required such as voltage and current sensors, gate drivers and power supplies to drive and control the semiconductor switches. This digest presents a hybrid circuit breaker which has the capability to drive the semiconductor switches on its own without having any additional DC power supplies or gate drivers. Validation of the circuit was done through experimental results. The experimental work has resulted in a 2 ms disconnection with negligible arc for a 100 A current in a DC loop with a 60 V DC power source, compared to a commercially available mechanical breaker with an approximate 3.25 ms break time with a severe arc.

articleTitle: Short-Circuit Faults in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Short circuit currents in inverter and converter-based resources connected to a common DC bus can be very different from typical sinusoidal AC based fault currents and inductive DC circuits. Inverter-based resources (IBR's) and converter-based resources (CBR's) are commonly used in DC microgrid applications resulting in highly capacitive networks. Faults can produce waveshapes that are significantly different than those from traditional AC or DC systems. These faults are analyzed to determine rates-of-rise (di/dt) and peak current values for a DC bus architecture. Fault currents were compared between a simulation model and experimental measurements for two different types of capacitors that could be commonly used in inverters and converters. These capacitors were used to represent inverters and converters connected to a DC microgrid bus structure. High frequency and low frequency, impedance measurements of the bus structure and capacitors were obtained to develop a system SPICE model which was used to illustrate the effects of fault current risetime on current waveshape. The rate-of-rise (di/dt) of the short-circuit current can be used to provide guidance for developing new standards and for providing engineers with practical information for developing DC circuit breakers and other DC protection equipment.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Decentralized Energy Management System for Undersupplied EV Charging Parks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, an energy management system (EMS) for undersupplied EV charging parks is presented. This undersupply is due to the maximum power demand for all charging stations connected to a common DC grid being larger than the maximum in feed power from AC mains. The EMS is completely decentralized and therefore allows easy addition of additional participants like chargers, AC/DC converters or storage systems into the common DC grid. This decentralization requires changes to the control structure of the connected power converters. These changes are evaluated for their effect on the stability of the whole grid. To investigate the proposed EMS, a simulation model based on real world charging park data is set up. The model is then used to evaluate the EMS for different degrees of undersupply and buffer storage. The findings are evaluated for different performance indicators to show the trade off between peak power shaving, installed storage and the charging of EVs.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Semiconductor-Based Isolation for Electric Vehicle Chargers in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, converters with semiconductor-based isolation for the application of electric vehicle (EV) charging in DC-microgrids are introduced. A PLECS circuit simulation model is set up to examine the fault behavior of those converters in comparison to standard isolated and non-isolated topologies. Three different fault scenarios are evaluated and influence of the converter topology on the system behavior is examined. It is shown that the semiconductor-based isolating converter has a similar behavior to the standard isolating converter considering systemic faults.

articleTitle: A Novel Cost-Effective Controller Hardware-in-The-Loop (CHIL) Test for SSCB Coordination in DC Microgrid Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: DC microgrid systems are recently utilized in power systems, and the significance of solid-state circuit breakers (SSCB) is paramount due to the absence of zero-crossing current in DC systems. Moreover, the coordination of a DC grid poses a challenge for these systems, primarily due to safety concerns. Consequently, the design of a test platform for monitoring the system's behavior in challenging situations holds significant importance. This paper presents an examination of a DC microgrid through a novel, easy to implement, and cost-effective controller hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) test platform designed using the MATLAB/ Simulink software and Python code. To evaluate the proposed platform, three test scenarios involving short circuits in different locations are investigated. The extracted CHIL results for each scenario is presented.

articleTitle: Grid supporting nonlinear control for AC-coupled DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Direct Current (DC) Microgrids have risen as a good option for better integrating distributed renewable energies and various highly dynamic DC loads, such as electrical vehicle supply equipment or industrial grids. However, for the large-scale deployment of such DC Microgrids, developing enhanced control strategies for these inverter-based, highly dynamic grids is crucial. The present paper introduces an innovative nonlinear control tailored for DC Microgrids supporting Alternative Current (AC) grids. Building upon existing methods, we extend the nonlinear control paradigm by incorporating multiple batteries and an AC link. This integration not only bolsters support for the AC grid, but also enhances the stability of DC voltage. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through experimental evaluations conducted on a Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) DC Microgrid configuration and compare it to a cascaded PI controller based on a linearized model.

articleTitle: A 380VDC/20A Bidirectional Solid State Circuit Breaker Using a Single GaN Four Quadrant Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Conventional bidirectional solid state circuit breaker (SSCB) designs use two back-to-back connected semiconductor switches to conduct current and block voltage in either direction. This paper presents the design and experimental results of a 380VDC/20A bidirectional solid state circuit breaker using a single GaN four quadrant switch (FQS) recently developed by Transphorm. The 650V FQS (TP65F060WS) serves as the main static switch in the SSCB. The SSCB is tested in a capacitor discharge circuit to characterize its reaction time and current conduction in forward and reverse polarity. A double pulse test is conducted to confirm the turn off characteristics and observe its turn on reactions. The results indicate that this new FQS is an excellent choice for future SSCB designs with significant component count reduction.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis and Simulation Study on Modular Resonant-Type Solid State Transformers in DC Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Traditional line frequency transformers are robust and can safely handle several over-current of several times the rated current during short circuit faults. As the grid is modernized and dc distribution is gaining popularity, power electronics converters are replacing the traditional line frequency transformers because of higher power density and better efficiency. However, they are more susceptible to failure during short circuit faults. Hence it is required to analyze and consider the effects of faults on the power electronic transformer-based systems in grid applications. This work focuses on the simulation of modular resonant dc solid state transformer (DC-SST) topology based on CLLC converter during short circuit faults.

articleTitle: An Open-Source Programmable DC/DC Converter for DC Nanogrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This work presents the design, development, and deployment of a DC nanogrid that is built from an open-source, programmable DC/DC converter. The DC/DC converter, named the Atverter, is programmable using the Arduino programming language, which facilitates ease-of-use and flexible functionality. Moreover, a Raspberry Pi can be utilized as a high-level tertiary controller for coordinating the dynamics of multiple Atverters connected in a DC nanogrid configuration. The results suggest the Atverter's viability as a useful programmable power converter that can be utilized by non-experts, students, and hobbyists in the DC nanogrid product space.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Series Arc Faults in DC Microgrids Using Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents experimental findings on the behavior of series arc faults within an MW-level DC microgrid when an inverter drive with variable frequency control and protective functions powers an induction motor. The experiments show that the series arc faults quenches when the inverter drive controlled for specific functions is in the circuit. The hypothesis points to the protective feature implemented in the inverter control against detrimental transients caused by a sudden loss of the DC source. The inverter supplies power to an induction motor rated at 75 HP (55.95 kW) and 460 V. The results demonstrate a promising approach to mitigate series arc faults by leveraging conventional inverters commonly found in DC microgrids.

articleTitle: DC Microgrid Control using a Multi-Function Multi-Domain Image-based Hierarchical Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study presents a digital twin framework for operational management of DC microgrids through the integration of multi-function, multi-domain digital images within the hierarchical digital twin structure. Digital images depict various aspects of physical assets at different levels of fidelity. The frame-work allows the hierarchical digital twin to respond to decision maker queries, offering estimations and analysis. A real-time simulation case study showcases the practical implementation of this approach and demonstrates its potential to enhance decision making and operational management of DC microgrids.

articleTitle: Integral Sliding Mode Controlled 3L-ANPC Based Bidirectional AFE Converter for DC Micro grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, an integral sliding mode controller is proposed for a bidirectional 3-level ANPC-based Active Front End (AFE) converter. An integral error term is added to the control law to reduce the steady state error and chattering. Thus, the reference tracking performance of the controller is improved. The high-frequency space vector PWM technique is used for the bidirectional 3-level AFE. Considering the output waveforms with low THD of the 3-level ANPC, only L filters are used at the converter output. The whole system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The obtained simulation results show that the proposed system provides high transient response and zero steady state error. Besides, the grid current harmonics are low in both directions of operation.

articleTitle: Unified Machine Learning Based Fault Detection Strategy Through Voltage-Sensing for Both AC and DC Side Faults in Photovoltaic Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) farms, consisting of a vast number of solar panels, are widely recognized as a viable source of renewable power generation. However, fault detection and protection remain critical challenges in PV farms. Conventional methods such as over-current relays prove to be inadequate, leading to system disruptions. The intricate nature of PV arrays necessitates fast fault detection. This paper proposes a unified machine learning based approach which can detect various types of faults on both DC (PV) and AC (grid) sides, using just one voltage sensor per each side. Moreover, our proposed approach offers a viable solution for fault detection, classification, and protection solution in a unified framework. The proposed method has been evaluated with a simulation case study of a 500kW grid-connected PV farm model and achieves 94.33% accuracy in fault detection on AC side while could perfectly detect faults on the DC side.

articleTitle: On the Effectiveness of Faulty DC Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) have attracted considerable attention in recent years. Many improvements have been achieved in these devices, particularly concerning aspects such as speed, voltage ratings, efficiency, and size. However, the study of DCCBs reliability, one of the most important challenges, remains unexploited and thus requires further research. So far, most research has focused on overcoming command error-related failures to trip or unintended tripping, paying little to no attention to physical failure of the DCCB components. If DCCB components fail, the fault current range will further increase, raising great safety concerns. This paper aims to analyze the impact that individual faults on the main component categories of the DCCB will have on the remaining components and the DC system where the DCCB is inserted. To conduct this study, a solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) inserted in a DC microgrid was considered. Two failure modes, taking place in the semiconductors and in the surge arrester components, were studied: open-circuit and short-circuit faults.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Modeling of Droop-Controlled Systems for Bus Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: With the rise of DC microgrids which commonly use droop control to control power sharing among multiple sources, there is a need to create a frequency domain model to study and analyze the stability of systems operating under droop control. In this paper an impedance-based frequency domain analytical model was created for a generalized DC microgrid system operating under droop control to analyze common bus stability. For the model, the open loop terminal impedances and various transfer functions were determined using a modified unterminated two-port g-parameter model. Using these transfer functions, the closed loop terminal impedances were determined by closing and internalizing each control path and adding the effect of droop control. To validate the analytical model, the terminal impedances of the analytical model were compared to simulated results obtained from Simulink via perturbation and linearization. Using this model, the bus stability of a four-converter system and the effects of control parameters on common bus impedance were analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamical Characterization of STATCOM Application: Applying Computer-Optimized Orthogonal Perturbations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) have become important devices in grid-connected applications to provide reactive power support and improve power quality. Studies have shown that STATCOMs can be efficiently analyzed and adaptively controlled based on a certain set of frequency responses. As most STATCOMs are complex and strongly time varying in their operation, realtime methods applying wideband identification techniques have become popular in obtaining these transfer functions. In the methods, an external voltage or current perturbation is added, for example, to the controller reference, and Fourier techniques are applied to the measured current and voltage responses to extract the spectral information. The challenge in a STATCOM application is that the variables are often coupled, and typically the system is very sensitive to external signals thus limiting the available methods to measure the frequency responses. This paper proposes computer-optimized orthogonal perturbations to measure the desired frequency responses for a STATCOM application. Due to orthogonality, the perturbations make it possible to simultaneously measure several coupled frequency responses. In addition, the perturbation spectrum can be optimized so that the energy is maximized at user- defined frequencies without increasing the signal time-domain amplitude. Therefore, the perturbations are well suited to STATCOM applications. Experimental measurements are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Review of Medium-Voltage Direct Current Distribution Technologies at ARPA-E
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper provides a retrospective of the BREAKERS and CABLES projects related to the protection, coordination, and hardware realization of medium-voltage direct current technologies at the Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy (ARPA-E) of the U.S. Department of Energy. These projects were funded to enable transformative advances in direct current (DC) medium-voltage (MV) microgrids and distribution systems. To do this they focus on rapid fault current identification and interruption as well as novel distribution of electrical power through lightweight medium-voltage cable systems free from damaging partial discharge. The paper includes a discussion of ARPA-E problem framing and the goals of transformative research, discussions on projects that make use of key enabling technologies such as wide bandgap semiconductors, optimal design procedures, and novel insulating and cooling methods that were developed for DC protection systems, cables, and connectors in these projects. A comparative analysis of with publicly available information for CABLES projects with commercial state-of-the-art technologies is included to provide context for the progress made to date. Finally, the distinct pathways that these technologies are taking to transition to the market are discussed.

articleTitle: SiC MOSFET with Embedded Current Sensor for SSCB Application - Enabeling Real Time Dynamic SOA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Fault protection of AC and DC network using semiconductors requires accurate electro-thermal design of active and passive devices to keep power losses low in nominal condition and to sustain high current overload. A Semiconductor Active Limiter Protection function has been designed using SiC MOSFET with embedded Current and Temperature Sensor. Both current and temperature sensors have been measured in real operating conditions. An experimental validation of the benefits of iMOSFET for ultra-fast current overload detection and protection is shown. Real time SiC MOSFET temperature monitoring is demonstrated. Using iMOSFET devices open a way towards real time dynamic SOA control.

articleTitle: Experimental Performance Validation of Z-Source DC Circuit Breaker for High Impedance Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Z-source DC circuit breakers (ZSCB's) provide automatic fault interruption without requiring sense and trip electronics. Further enables for rapid fault interruption with simple and less complex circuitry. However, the circuit breaker's minimum detectable fault ramp rate restricts the widespread use of ZSCBs. This limitation hinders the ZSCB's performance for protecting against high impedance short circuit faults and overload events. The effective solution of incorporating current sensors and an auxiliary branch with a power electronic switch has already been proposed in the literature. However, the proposed method has not been experimentally verified at higher system voltages and currents to validate the circuit breaker's performance. This paper describes the control strategy of the solution implemented with a modified Q-Z-Source circuit breaker (MQZSCB) and presents experimental results to support the circuit breaker's performance for high impedance faults considering more electric aircraft (MEA) standardized voltage rating of 270 V DC and at nominal current of 10 A with a preset fault current value of 20 A.

articleTitle: Energy Source Integration with Storage Systems via a Multiport Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Microgrids represent an innovative approach to improving energy supply systems' resilience, efficiency and sustainability. Integrating multiple power sources is critical for this purpose, and bidirectional converters play a central role in this process by facilitating the transfer of power in any direction and the incorporation of multiple power inputs. This study examines the efficiency of a multiport converter, whose function is to aggregate various power sources and dynamically adapt the load distribution to optimise performance in real time. Meticulous optimisation of the multiport converter efficiency and load control mechanisms significantly reduce the voltage on the primary grid. This strategic intervention contributes to mitigating congestion and strengthens the electrical infrastructure's overall stability

articleTitle: Distributed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Agents for Real-Time Energy Management of DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents a real-world military use of a microgrid with Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V). This plug-and-play system delivers efficient, fast-deploying power for a contingency base within 20 minutes, generating up to 500 kW of three-phase power. It utilizes vehicle-based Internal Combustion (IC) engine generators and an Energy Storage System (ESS) to power vehicle equipment and off-board loads like shelters and communication centers. However, fluctuating off-board loads create operational challenges for this V2G-V2V microgrid. This work proposes a real-time implementation of energy management based on distributed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), a deep reinforcement learning, to address this problem for continuous state and continuous action spaces. This work formulates the energy management problem as a Markov decision process, considering random load demands and fuel costs. This paper aims to minimize the microgrid's operating costs by optimizing the dispatch of onboard vehicle power generators and storage units. With simulation experiments, this work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed distributed deep reinforcement learning approach. The results show the distributed DDPG agents can utilize the state of the ESS and significantly decrease the microgrid's overall operation costs. This validates the practical value of distributed DDPG for economic operations in military microgrids.

articleTitle: Design Considerations of Modular Multilevel Converters in Bidirectional Energy-Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Bidirectional energy-storage systems have become important elements in many renewable-energy applications to control power fluctuations between the energy source and the power grid. Recently, modular multilevel converters (MMCs) integrated with energy storage have become attractive solutions in such applications. They exhibit low harmonic distortion, improved fault tolerance, and faster response compared to traditional solutions. These qualities make MMCs well-suited for grid-connected applications, where maintaining stable and high-quality power is required. This work presents a novel approach to design and optimize the operation of a MMC connected to energy-storage. In the work, the energy-storage type, semiconductor devices, and control strategy are selected so that an efficient system operation is guaranteed. Simulation results are shown and used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Enabling MVDC PV Collection Grids with Modular Solid State Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Solar energy is typically collected through AC grids because of strong reliability and availability of standard solutions. The introduction of Solid State Transformers may not only allow reducing footprint and losses, but also implement peak shaving capabilities and the injection to MVDC grids directly. This work proposes an innovative PV energy collecting strategy with modular isolated DC/DC converters.

articleTitle: Hybrid and Solid State Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: U.S. Navy ships need more electric power for increased capability, automation, mobility, lethality, and they need increased operating efficiency for reduced fuel costs. This is motivating the adoption of Direct Current power distribution systems. The voltage range is from 1 kV to 12 kV or greater (LVDC to MVDC), and the steady state current range is up to 5 kA. DC circuit breakers operate faster than A C breakers since they circumvent the current zero-crossing requirement of A C breakers. Protective DC switchgear is a key element in a DC power distribution system that provides electric power reliably and cost-effectively, utilizing more efficient, high-power sources, energy storage, and transmission. For over 25 years, Diversified Technologies Inc (DTI) has been designing and building high-voltage DC circuit breakers capable of multi-kA switching at voltages up to and greater than 100 kV DTI has shipped and qualified for military applications hundreds of systems. These switches are well-suited for shipboard DC circuit breaker applications. This paper describes on-going hybrid and solid state circuit breaker development at DTI.

articleTitle: Selection of Supercapacitor Banks for Renewable Energy-Based DC-Operable Refrigerators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Inverter-driven white goods are generally based on an internal DC bus to drive the brushless DC motor units and the auxiliary circuits. Given that the AC line-derived DC bus is easily accessible, a renewable energy DC source can be used to power, by removing the rectifiers. However, when a renewable energy source is the primary energy supply, its fluctuating nature requires an energy storage system. To avoid the use of batteries with a short life cycle, supercapacitors become a very good alternative. However, given that the price of supercapacitors is still higher than a battery pack, and they may come with lower energy density, we need to optimize the size of the bank. This paper investigates the potential of a supercapacitor-assisted low-frequency converter technique and the sizing of supercapacitor modules of a supercapacitor-assisted DC refrigerator project.

articleTitle: A Solid-State Circuit Breaker Configuration with Reduced Energy Dissipation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Current literature provides a reasonable set of DC circuit breaker (DCCB) topologies to integrate protection capability within DC distribution systems, namely Solid-State Circuit Breakers (SSCBs), Hybrid Circuit Breakers (HCBs) and Mechanical Circuit Breakers (MCBs). SSCBs are an interesting option to provide protection for emerging energy distribution systems, such as DC microgrids, since they are fast acting and precise, being particularly suitable for low voltage systems, where their on-state losses are negligible. Despite the many improvements proposed in the literature regarding topics such as switching speeds, cost of implementation and power losses, the risk of failure of sensitive components integrated within SSCBs is often overlooked when the scientific community presents novel SSCB structures. Some of the most important SSCBs components include the energy dissipating elements, protecting the semiconductors from transient overvoltages. To curtail the risk of failures in pivotal SSCB components, particularly in metal oxide varistors (MOVs), this paper proposes a SSCB featuring reduced energy dissipation requirements and, ultimately, reduced risk of MOV failure.

articleTitle: Design of a Cell String Level Maximum Power Point Tracking Converter Connected to a DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The presented research focuses on the design and implementation of a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) system for photovoltaic (PV) panels installed on a sailing yacht. This yacht relies solely on renewable energy sources, particularly solar energy when anchored. The unique challenge addressed is the impact of partial shading on the PV panels due to the yacht's masts and sails. A two-step conversion system is developed, where string-level converters adjust to shading conditions to maintain optimal power output. The isolated converter then steps up the voltage for integration into a bipolar DC grid. Experimental results demonstrate that this system significantly enhances energy yield under varying shading conditions.

articleTitle: A Study on Efficiency Improvement of Power Flow Control Using Four-Switch Buck-Boost Converter Focusing on Phase Shift
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, we study the efficiency improvement of power flow control using four-switch buck-boost converters (FSBBCs). The power flow control in DC power networks has been studied so far using some bidirectional DC-DC converters. As one of the converters, FSBBC has been used as the power flow controller, and the effectiveness of the power flow control has been investigated. For implementing the power flow control using FSBBC, two operational modes, 2SW mode, and 4SW mode, need to be used. In 4SW operation mode, it is possible to arbitrarily set the phase shift of the switching of the arms. The phase shift does not affect the amount of power flow but affects the ripple and root-mean-square (RMS) value of the inductor current. Therefore, the phase shift affects the efficiency. This paper studies the efficiency improvement by considering the phase shift and proposes a simple and easy modulation method to achieve an appropriate phase shift and improve the efficiency of the power flow control. Experimental results validate the effectiveness.

articleTitle: Operating Range Analysis of Dual Active Bridge Converters in FRT-Buck Modulation Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The FRT-Buck modulation of three-phase dual active bridge (DAB3) converters features soft-switching characteristics and current-limiting capability, which is a critical approach to realizing fault ride-through (FRT) operation of DC distribution grids. In this paper, the operating ranges of DAB3 converters under FRT-Buck modulation are first studied. According to current limitations, this paper divides the operating ranges of DAB3 converters into three different types. Then, the operating trajectories of DAB3 are studied under different operating conditions. In addition, the heat map of transmission power is given under constraints. Finally, the actual peaking values of three-phase currents and elliptical operating trajectories are validated on the MATLAB/Simulink platform. The simulation results confirm the accuracy of the theoretical derivation. The proposed method can determine the operating point of the DAB3 in post-fault operations and assist the design of protection schemes for DC distribution grids.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of DC Space Microgrids Using a Markov Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach to assess the reliability of a space microgrid architecture for long-term space exploration and human presence. It considers internal and external microgrid faults and disturbances, along with their effects on the functionality of a space habitat. The paper presents a quantitative reliability assessment model for a space microgrid using a Markov model. Simulation results for various disturbance scenarios in a space habitat model are used to study the different failure modes of the power system components. Simulations are also used to evaluate various fault repair schedules and assess the system's reliability during various phases of operation.

articleTitle: Issues in Practical Impedance Measurement of Li-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Li-ion batteries have become extensively applied in various consumer products and power-distribution systems. The increased use of the batteries have raised environmental issues as most of the used batteries are landfilled instead of recycled upon reaching end of life. The reusability of a battery can be evaluated by applying the battery state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH). While it is difficult to directly measure these quantities, the battery internal impedance can be measured to obtain the SOC and SOH. Recent studies have shown real-time methods based on broadband perturbations such as pseudorandom binary sequence (PRBS) to rapidly and accurately obtain the impedance. However, the presented methods are often sensitive to external noise which can lead to false battery characterization. This work presents some of the main sources of measurement errors and proposes techniques to minimize their effect. Experimental measurements based on a commercial Li-ion battery is presented and used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: Novel Device for Fast Detection and Limitation of Short-Circuit Currents in LVDC Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-destructive device for detecting and limiting short-circuit currents in LVDC grids. The proposed solution is based on the concept of using a transformer fully saturated by a permanent magnet during normal operation. When a short circuit condition occurs, the transformer desaturates, triggering the detection and protection mechanism. The function and structure of the unit as well as design criteria are explained. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the device in detecting and limiting overcurrents. This hardware-based detection solution is particularly suitable for being installed in a semiconductor circuit breaker rated up to but not limited to 100 A.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life digital shadow for an eVTOL Powertrain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study introduces a real-time digital shadow representation for an electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) powertrain, aimed at estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of key components. Leveraging real-time operational data, the digital shadow dynamically updates RUL estimates. The objective of this digital shadow is to enhance the reliability and maintenance strategies for eVTOL systems. The implementation encompasses critical components, including DC link capacitors, the motor, and the battery. Experimental results demonstrate the capability of the digital shadow to adjust RUL estimates in real-time in response to operational condition changes.

Author Keywords: electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) vehicle

articleTitle: Study on Conversion from an Existing Alternating Current Medium-Voltage Line to a Direct Current Line: A Case of Load or Source Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Simultaneous increase of power generation through renewable systems and load due owing to the rapid growth in electrified road transportation systems, leads to new challenges in the design, operation, and protection of distribution-level electrical power systems. This paper addresses challenges related to the integration of new sources or loads to a distribution grid through long alternating current lines. The International Council on Large Electric Systems medium-voltage benchmark model developed for North America was used for simulation studies. Use cases were developed to illuminate the issues related to long alternating current lines and the usefulness of medium-voltage direct current lines in a distribution network.

articleTitle: FEA-Driven Solutions to Minimize Driving Loop Inductance and EMI in MHz PCB Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The gate driver parasitic loop inductance and EMI characteristics of a 1-MHz, 1-kW GaN buck converter are investigated. The parasitic effects contributed by PCB traces are critical in higher-power and MHz-frequency operational systems. These parasitic inductances lead to voltage overshoots and ringing, which is a primary cause of EMI. Therefore, the power and driving loops within the layout were designed to minimize loop inductances. The parasitic inductances, extracted through finite element analysis (FEA) tools, were modelled within LTspice to assess the impacts of the designed layout. The gate-to-source voltage waveform from the hardware exhibits slightly higher voltage spikes compared to the LTspice simulation. The conducted noise measured in the FEA was over the standard electromagnetic compliance limit by 10 dBuV in the frequency range of 1 MHz to 5 MHz. Adding a filter to the input side of the converter will improve the conducted emissions.

articleTitle: Business Case of Green Energy Based End to End DC Power Networks: Extremely Fast DC Charging of Electrical Vehicles Near Highways
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The major issue with the existing legacy alternating current (AC)-based power grid is to extend AC power flow control and converter topologies to the new direct current (DC) based renewable generation, storage and dynamic loads. An innovative concept of the end-to-end DC power-based extremely fast charging (XFC) EV architecture is introduced in this paper. The open question is how to implement DC networks for large-scale applications and justify a business case for such networks. Compared to the existing AC grid with multiple AC-to-DC and DC-to-AC conversion stages our proposed architecture can save more than 25% of power losses and about 30% cost savings of EV chargers depending on voltage and power levels. In this work, we will also demonstrate that without connecting with the AC grid we can effectively set up a parallel DC infrastructure for newer EV charging loads.

Author Keywords: End to End DC Power Networks

articleTitle: Compact GaN-Based 25kW, 480V Three-Level Active Front End Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Interface units are needed to connect DC microgrids to the AC grid. This paper presents a compact and high-efficiency 25kW 480V Gallium Nitride (GaN) based bidirectional Three-Level Active-Neutral-Point-Clamped (3L-ANPC) converter for DC microgrids. The entire system, including the FPGA, DC-link capacitors, switching devices in the topology, and AC grid inductive filters, is integrated onto a single board. The 3L-ANPC topology provides balanced distribution of power losses and voltage stress among the switches. A 200kHz switching frequency is used for the GaN devices to reduce the size of passive elements. A PCB-based DC busbar is designed to minimize inductance, ensure a compact size, and reduce parasitic capacitances. Additionally, PCB-based inductors are designed to minimize size and tolerance on inductance value and reduce magnetic flux pollution in the converter. System control is performed using an Intel ultra-high-speed FPGA. Simulation and experimental results validate the electrical and thermal performance of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Output Impedance Measurement of Digitally Controlled Power Converters in LVDC-Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Due to the increase in possible sector couplings to local low voltage DC grids, the amount of controlled infeed converters connected to the grids increases. For these grids to remain stable, proper system analysis is required. While simulation of these systems is possible, the final setup requires measurements. In this paper, the problem of output impedance measurement of digitally controlled power converters, which make up the majority of infeed converters in medium to high power LVDC grids, is discussed. Digital control leads to several requirements regarding the test signals used to measure the converters. Due to the nonlinearity of certain power converter types, the measurements required for a full description of the power converter typically need to be taken for a variety of loads and grid voltages. Wide bandwidth measurements can be used to reduce the overall measurement time. These wide bandwidth measurements require further investigation regarding signal amplitude, which is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Modeling and Energy Management Optimization of a Hybrid Electric Ferry with DC Power Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: New hybrid and electric propulsion and power systems challenge the conventional diesel engine propulsion commonly used in ships due to stricter emission regulations, increased fuel prices, and technological advancements in power electronics. Ferries with hybrid power systems and direct current distribution are gaining more interest due to their ability to reduce fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. The detailed modeling of hybrid electric propulsion systems presented in this paper can provide valuable insights into the development and implementation of these systems in ferries. In addition, the study includes an evaluation of three different energy management systems for the hybrid ferry system and discusses their simulation results.

articleTitle: Exploration of Use-Case-Dependent Modeling Approach for Distributed DC-Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, the previously described Use-Case-Dependent Modeling Approach is evaluated and its usefulness for grid simulation is explored. One of the main merits of the approach is its application in automated system analysis. Previous results also suggest a reduced usage of computing resources. This however has not yet been systematically tested and properly verified. Therefore, to inspect the validity of this approach, the methodology is explained and simulation results are compared to measurements of the modeled DC system. It is shown that the grid models adequately represent the system's behavior and the simulation results can therefore be used for system analysis. Discrepancies can be explained by an insufficient modeling of the measured system's damping elements. These differences are however small enough to be mitigated by usually applied error margins, especially for system stability analysis. Although more work is required for full verification, the validity and versatility of the approach is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of a Modular Marine DC Microgrid Testbed with Controller-Hardware-in-the-Loop (CHIL) for Real-Time Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Integration of renewable sources enables economical and sustainable energy availability to coastal and remote communities. Different power electronics converters deliver electric power from renewable sources to the local communities. A Multi-Port Converter (MPC) is utilized to allow energy flow between subsystems in a controlled, efficient, and safe manner. This paper proposes the incorporation of multiple MPCs in a modular manner to allow extensive integration of renewable sources, loads, and energy sources. A DC microgrid testbed is developed to evaluate the performance of two proposed MPCs. The individual converters of each MPC are initially designed and developed in a Simulink/PLECS simulation environment. The average model of designed converters is further tested in Typhoon real-time simulator with Controller Hardware In Loop (CHIL) mode for high fidelity converter operation. The individual converters are integrated into their respective MPCs and operated in close-loop control through MPC control algorithms. Eventually, a plant control algorithm is designed to control the proposed DC microgrid testbed. Typhoon real-time CHIL simulation results are provided to validate the operation of each converter and the whole microgrid in the testbed.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of a Droop-Controlled DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Stable operation is a primary performance metric that a DC microgrid system should satisfy. This paper presents a comprehensive stability analysis for a two-converter system attached to a Constant Power Load (CPL) under droop control. The study establishes the stability criteria and calculates the minimum capacitance required for the stable operation of the system. The study considers the virtual inertia incorporated via a low-pass filter (LPF) to avoid sudden voltage fluctuations in the analysis. It is concluded that an optimum value of virtual inertia can reduce the required capacitance for stable operation. Additionally, the paper derives a relation providing the maximum power transfer limit for given system parameters and the effect of virtual inertia on this limit. The results are verified by simulation in MATLAB/Simulink. These findings have practical implications for designing and operating DC microgrid systems, particularly for optimizing virtual inertia for maximum power transfer while ensuring system stability.

articleTitle: Heuristic Evolutionary Optimization for Control and Management of Renewable-Based Hybrid Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The surge in renewable energy and distributed generation necessitates advanced control systems for network performance enhancement. However, the lack of a standardized evaluation framework hampers comparisons, especially in complex hybrid networks. Hybrid energy systems offer greener and more reliable networks but require sophisticated control methods. To address this challenge, research explores novel linear and nonlinear techniques. This overview focuses on heuristic evolutionary optimization methods for Microgrids, covering AC, DC, and hybrid AC-DC systems, highlighting current research and future control requirements.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian Surface Shaping Power Flow Modeling and Control Design of DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A new paradigm in DC microgrid modeling and control has become more and more necessary due to the increasingly dynamic nature of sources, loads, and storage. Many conventional methods face difficulties when dealing with the nonlinearities and uncertainties that naturally exist in these systems. Emerging as a powerful alternative, Hamiltonian Surface Shaping and Power Flow Control (HSSPFC) offers a robust and elegant approach to navigating these complexities. Using the rich framework of Hamiltonian mechanics, this approach shapes the energy surface of the system and guides the flow of power along desired trajectories with minimal effort and guaranteed stability. This offers exciting possibilities for the efficient and resilient operation of DC microgrids, enabling seamless integration of renewables and paving the way for a new generation of distributed energy systems. This paper will present the general methodology and procedures for using the HSSFPC tools in the modeling, control, and analysis of a DC microgrid.

articleTitle: Economical Pathway of Adopting Single-Phase Induction Motors in Emerging DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A major practical challenge in adopting highly advantageous DC microgrids is related to the deployment or displacement of the low-cost small single-phase induction motors (SPIMs) in millions of home or industrial appliances. Power electronic inverters are generally required to generate AC voltages from the DC grids (e.g., 380VDC) to drive AC motors, creating a prohibitive cost barrier. This paper reviews various types of small SPIMs in the market today as well as the inverter topologies and control strategies used to drive them from a DC bus. Key enabling technologies, including low-cost monolithic inverter power ICs, Sensorless motor control, and peak current limiting control, are then identified to overcome such cost barrier while enhancing functionalities and performance, such as improved efficiency, better starting torque, reduced noise, and variable speed control. The objective is to explore technological pathways for transitioning from single-phase AC motors powered by AC grids today to single-phase AC motors powered by DC microgrids in the near future. Ultimately, the goal is to achieve lower-cost, higher-performance three-phase induction motors powered cost-effectively by DC microgrids.

articleTitle: USB-C Outlets for Plug Loads in 350V DC Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: USB-C has become the universal plug standard for charging consumer electronics, typically through AC/DC wall adapters. As new standards in USB power distribution allow USB-C ports to provide up to 240W at 48V, many discuss the possibility of USB-C emerging as a plug-load standard, especially in DC buildings. This work proposes the use of USB-C wall outlets to power the emerging USB-C ecosystem without need for a wall adapter. We first study the market feasibility of USB-C outlets through a series of customer discovery interviews. We then perform several experiments to evaluate the technical feasibility. These include a comparative evaluation of efficiency and a thermal experiment to study how the heat from outlet's conversion loss can be dissipated through an exterior wall section.

articleTitle: Hybrid Modulation Scheme for CLLC Resonant Converter with Ultra-Wide Voltage Range for V2G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid modulation scheme consisting of phase-shift modulation (PSM) and pulse-frequency modulation (PFM) for a CLLC resonant converter for vehicle charging applications in DC Microgrids is proposed. To increase the operating range of the converter, an iterative design process of the converter is introduced. PSM, as a conventional alternative to PFM, can be used to further increase the operating range and improve the efficiency at light-load conditions. Since the converter in vehicle-to-grid (V2G) applications oftentimes operates under light-load conditions, implementing this hybrid modulation scheme can increase the efficiency dramatically. A novel idea of mode switching is also proposed in the paper to ensure smooth mode transitions. The working principle of this modulation scheme and the efficiency analysis were investigated in PLECS.

articleTitle: Direct Coupling of Solar Plants and Electrolyzers with Voltage-Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Hydrogen produced from renewable energies such as photovoltaic (PV) is a valuable option for decarbonization. Conventional solar plants use voltage-source converters that interconnect PV arrays with an electrical grid. The converters transfer DC power into an AC power grid. As opposed to a conventional renewable plant coupled with an AC grid, this work discusses systems that directly couple PV arrays with electrolyzers. Such systems may range up to several megawatts or even more per unit. System design aspects, power converters, and the operation of multiple electrolyzers are analyzed and discussed with a focus on efficiencies. In this context, the single-phase dual active bridge is considered as an isolated DC-to-DC converter in a voltage range up to 2000 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf>.

articleTitle: Two-Phase Cooling Solution for SiC/GaN Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Power modules are crucial components in power converters for various applications like DC microgrids. We propose to improve thermal performance of SiC/GaN power modules using an integrated two-phase mini-channel cold plate that is scalable in physical dimensions to match commercially available power modules. The proposed configuration integrates the mini-channel cold plate within the module baseplate, eliminating the thermal interface material conventionally used between module and cold plate, resulting in a reduced overall thermal resistance. Additionally, the introduced structure incorporates porous channel walls and a micro-gap connecting adjacent mini-channels. These additions enhance stability and power dissipation of flow boiling, which is a heat transfer process that occurs during the boiling of a liquid, typically water, in a channel or a tube over a heated surface. The thermal performance of the proposed integrated porous mini-channel with micro-gap (IPMCMG) two-phase mini-channel cold plate is compared with a conventional mini-channel cold plate (CMC) operating under two-phase cooling regime. The experiment demonstrates a 30.5°C reduction in junction temperature for the IPMCMG compared to CMC, with a 453W or 56% increase in maximum power dissipation. At flow rates as low as 25 ml/min, stable flow boiling and minimal pressure drops are observed. The experimental findings for various flow rates demonstrate the notable enhancement in thermal performance achieved by IPMCMG, while maintaining a pressure drop similar to that of commercial cold plates. Utilizing a high-speed camera, the visualization of flow boiling in IPMCMG illustrates how porous micro-gaps applied to mini-channels effectively prevent local dry outs, the condition in which only the vapor phase is present in parts of the two-phase coldplate, leading to a fast, uncontrolled temperature increase, showcasing its effectiveness in managing two-phase flows and boosting heat dissipation. In power modules electrical short circuits cause severe thermal stress, given the high power dissipation. It is desirable for a power module to be able to withstand for some time a short circuit condition. A transient experiment conducted to simulate an electrical short circuit shows a promising increase in the time it takes for junction temperature to reach a critical failure point under short circuit conditions, showing a desirable feature of the proposed thermal solution.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance DC Microgrid Control Scheme with Li-Ion Battery System for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced DC micro grid to-pology and the respective control algorithm that provides en-hanced equalization and dynamic performance of the Li-ion bat-tery storage system (BSS) in electric vehicle applications. The sug-gested control scheme is a hybrid energy storage system that con-sists of Li-ion batteries for the main energy reservoir in back-to-back connection with an auxiliary energy storage system (AESS) of supercapacitors (SCs) or Li-ion battery cells. The AESS improves the battery cell-to-cell equalization and provides energy support to any weak or problematic cells and also, enhances the dynamic performance of the vehicle by providing reinforcing en-ergy during a fast vehicle acceleration and energy saving by ab-sorbing any excess energy during abrupt braking of the vehicle. The battery cell equalization is realized through the Cell Equalizer Controller (CEC). The energy flow through the AESS is managed by a DC-DC converter combined with a matrix switch system which connects the AESS with any battery cell that needs support detected by the Cell Ageing Estimator (CAE). Selective simulation results are presented to validate the operating improvements of the proposed DC micro grid control scheme with Li-ion battery.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Meshed DC Shipboard Power Systems Using Stochastic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In DC shipboard power systems (DC-SPS), the enhanced network complexity and high penetration of power electronic devices make the system level reliability a critical design aspect. This paper proposes a stochastic framework for the reliability assessment of DC-SPSs based on a three-stage Monte Carlo (MC) simulation, including component failure sampling, active fault propagation, and reliability index calculation. The proposed MC framework is verified for a simplified meshed DC grid through comparison with an analytical method. Later, the advantages of the MC method are demonstrated for a dynamic positioning vessel equipped with a ring-type DC power system architecture. The results quantify the impact of redundancy on the reliability of a DC-SPS, show the spread in the subsystem repair times, and reveal the system's availability during both the initialization and steady-state. Combined, the simulation results reveal the strengths and weaknesses of the designed grid, guiding the focus for future reliability enhancements.

articleTitle: A Techno-Economic Study of DC Microgrids for Electric School Bus Charging Depots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Solar canopy microgrids offer many benefits for electric school bus fleet charging depots. This work models and compares the 25-year life-cycle cost of several DC and AC microgrid topologies. Based on the results, grid-tied AC topologies cost the least today, but off-grid DC topologies may be the most economical in the future if the costs of electricity and interconnection agreements increase with the demand for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Effects of Switching Overvoltages in LVDC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Current interruption in an electrical distribution system, both in normal and fault conditions, may produce switching overvoltages because of non infinite short circuit power of the upstream supply system, namely due to system inductances (e.g. cable inductances) upstream the interruption point. This paper aims to demonstrate, through a system approach, how these overvoltages are generated during the switching phase of both traditional interruptive devices (i.e. ElectroMechanical Circuit Breakers and Fuses) and new technology interruptive devices (i.e. Solid-State Circuit Breakers) and how those overvoltages can affect the surrounding equipment in a LVDC Microgrid. In particular, this paper emphasizes the risk of unintentional tripping of the interruptive devices installed on adjacent feeders/incomers and potential damages to relevant equipment. Last, but not least, two different solutions to mitigate the negative effects of those overvoltages are presented.

articleTitle: Solid State Power Substation DC Node Optimization and Controller Hardware-In-The-Loop Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A solid state power substation (SSPS) node is a microgrid that integrates distributed energy resources and loads and injects/absorbs power to/from the SSPS distribution network. It is an essential building block of a futuristic distribution grid network. This paper presents the development and demonstration of optimization use cases of a SSPS DC node. By adopting multi-layer hierarchical control architecture and developing automatic device identification and dynamic optimization formulation algorithms, the SSPS DC node can perform plug-and-play resource integration and seamless transition of the optimized node operation under on and off grid condition without sophisticated algorithms, control mode changes, and user interactions. Four optimization use cases including economic dispatches with price signal changes, a sudden PV power drop, and a single directional meter and its associated costs with sending power back to the grid, and resiliency under a grid inverter trip condition were demonstrated through the real-time controller hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

articleTitle: Leakage Inductance and Turns-Ratio Optimization for Fixed Input Variable Output Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: An optimization procedure for leakage inductance and turns ratio selection of the fixed input variable output single phase-shift dual active bridge converter is presented. The procedure consists of determining the leakage inductance and turns ratio combination that will produce the lowest average semiconductor losses throughought the entire operating time. The time behavior of the output voltage is based on normal distribution and was generated through the inverse cumulative distribution function. A transformer with optimum leakage inductance and turns ratio was built to validate the procedure. The analytical RMS leakage inductance current was 16.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, resulting in a 5 % variation from the experimental value of 17.4 A.

articleTitle: Degradation and State of Health Prediction of a Battery Used in a Microgrid in Real-time
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Battery degradation is a complex physicochemical phenomenon intricately influenced by operational parameters and environmental factors. This paper delves into the degradation of lithium-ion batteries within microgrid systems, utilizing historical aging data from the University of Wisconsin-Madison to train a degradation model employing neural networks. The dataset is transformed to align with the battery pack rating pertinent to this investigation. The study identifies and examines several contributing factors to battery degradation, with a specific focus on temperature, charging current, discharging current, and depth of discharge. Emphasizing the significance of these parameters, particularly the latter three, the research endeavors to predict battery degradation in diverse operational conditions within a Microgrid system. This study modeled a Microgrid configuration capable of operating in islanded and grid-connected mode featuring solar PV, wind, a diesel generator, and a battery. Real-time simulations of different operational scenarios are conducted using the digital real-time simulator. Additionally, the battery's operational status is sent to a controller to predict its degradation and state of health. The controller used here is a Raspberry Pi, and communication is facilitated through UDP protocol.

articleTitle: Filtered Feedback Control on DC Microgrid to Power a High-Performance Battery-Based Cutter Dredger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In the marine industry, resilience and flexibility in use are among the most important targets to be attained. These two goals are even more crucial when considering specific vessels like cutter dredgers. The latter are in charge of providing the very specific function of soil removal, which constitutes a high-power load to be transiently powered from the onboard power plant. In this paper, a ring DC grid is proposed to exploit the presence of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in supplying the onboard loads of a dredger. An advanced control system on DC power electronics interfaces is designed to guarantee the power quality requirements while preserving the diesel units. A realistic load profile is considered in the synthesis of control functions, where a filtered feedback is adopted to optimally share the generating effort. Significant transients are discussed in order to demonstrate the control performance in managing power sources and BESS.

articleTitle: Supercapacitors for Enabling Mechanical Circuit Breakers in Shipboard Zonal Secondary DC-Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This article proposes a variant design philosophy for shipboard zonal secondary dc distribution systems. The main features of such a power system are the insertion of supercapacitor devices together with chopper power converters that enable the implementation of mechanical circuit breakers for feeder and bustie protection. Hence, an overview of low-voltage dc protection technologies and navy pulse power load applications are discussed. The proposed secondary single-line diagram establishes the feasibility of fault levels and, consequently, the implementation of mechanical circuit breakers. Then, a transient event is carried out to highlight the zonal electrical distribution system performance in terms of continuous power supply into the dc-grid secondary zones. Results show that supercapacitors located in dc-bus enhance the circuit's voltage time constant, allowing extended periods for opening and closing protection devices (controlled by a power management system) and increasing the grid survivability for critical impulsive loads.

articleTitle: A Power-Centric Digitally-Managed 48V Distribution Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Technologies such as USB and Ethernet can be used to power devices in buildings, but have burdens of cost and energy efficiency that make them unsuitable as a primary means of distributing power to most loads in buildings. This paper describes a proposed standard for 48V DC power distribution in buildings suitable for powering most loads in residential and commercial buildings. It includes both general data communication as well as communication for managing the distribution of power. The maximum power is targeted at 1000 W with options for low- and high-power circuits to minimize costs.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>This work was supported by the Assistant Secretary for Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, Building Technologies Office, of the U.S. Department of Energy under Contract No. DE-AC02-05CH11231.

articleTitle: Non-linear active disturbance rejection control for three-phase dual-active-bridge DC/DC converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sixth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The three-phase dual-active-bridge (DAB3) is the most promising converter topology of isolated bidirectional DC/DC converters in DC power systems. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) has gained research attention as voltage controller in DAB3 DC/DC converters. This paper proposes a non-linear ADRC (NL-ADRC) voltage controller for DAB3 DC/DC converters. Opposite to non-linear controllers for DAB3 converters, the developed controller achieves good performance, although its formulation is based on a simple DAB3 DC/DC converter model. This is achieved thanks to the estimation and rejection of the total disturbance, which includes converter model uncertainties. The application of the generalised ADRC concept and the employment of advanced estimation and feedback control methods in the ADRC model, for the first time in the case of DAB3 converters, bring benefits to the performance of the voltage controller. The effective disturbance rejection and nominal performance in dynamic and steady-state operation of the converter is demonstrated through results in frequency and time domains, as well as hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) tests. The effect of the control parameters is also analysed, to reveal the benefits of the proposed structure of the NL-ADRC model.
